title: Galectin-3 in Alzheimer's Disease, Linking Microglia Inflammation to Pathology
summary: The harmful behavior of microglia in the aging brain, and the mechanisms driving this behavior, has become a major focus for research into Alzheimer's disease. Microglia are innate immune cells resident in the central nervous system, involved in tissue maintenance in addition to defense against pathogens, analogous to the macrophages found elsewhere in the body. When microglia become overly inflammatory, as occurs in aging, this not only contributes to disruptive chronic inflammation in brain tissue, but also directly impairs the normal role of microglia in the maintenance of neural networks.…
